issues.description: Pixel format / bytes-per-pixel mismatch between the problem statement and the provided template/solution. The problem text explicitly states “High Color Modus mit 16 Bit pro Pixel (5 Bit Rot, 6 Bit Grün, 5 Bit Blau)”, but the template and the solution treat pixels as 32-bit (4 bytes) — e.g. buffer size display_start = RESB 8294400 (1920*1080*4), address arithmetic multiplies x by 4 and uses a scanline stride of 7680, and stores/loads a full 32-bit value with instructions like mov [addr], ecx / mov ecx, [esi]. The problem statement also instructs mov ecx, [esi] (a 32-bit load) while simultaneously stating 16-bit pixels. This contradiction will confuse students about how to compute the address (bytes-per-pixel and stride) and how to read/write pixel values, and will lead to incorrect implementations if they follow the problem text but use the template.
issues.suggested_fix:
Make the pixel format consistent across all artifacts. Two viable fixes:
1) If the intent is 32-bit pixels (as in template/solution): update the problem statement to describe True Color / 32 bits per pixel (and adjust any textual mentions of '16 Bit' and the 5-6-5 description). Update the example input description to match a 32-bit value (e.g. 0xAARRGGBB or 0x00RRGGBB) if relevant.
2) If the intent is 16-bit 5-6-5 High Color (as the problem currently states): change the template and solution to use 2 bytes per pixel — set display_start RESB to 1920*1080*2 (4147200), compute addresses using bytes-per-pixel = 2 (stride = 1920*2 = 3840), multiply x by 2 (or use addressing tricks), and read/write 16-bit values (e.g. use mov [addr], cx or mov word [addr], cx / mov cx, [addr]). Apply the same change to any input/output examples and comments so students have a single, consistent specification.
